sentences.text: T h is petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashment of FIR No.11 of 2022 for offences under Sections 506, 344, 376, 376(2)(n), 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(v) and 3(2)(va) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act registered at Police Station Saleha, District Panna (M.P.) and subsequent proceedings registered against the petitioners.

2. The case of the prosecution in short is that on 21.11.2021 the complainant Motilal Verma, lodged a missing report of his daughter namely Ku. Sapna Verma aged about 20 years with effect from 10.11.2021.
The prosecutrix was recovered on 12.01.2022.
Her statements under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C. have been recorded.

On that basis, offences under Sections 376, 376(2)(N), 344,
120-B and 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w-ii), 3(2-va) and 3(2- v) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act have been registered against the petitioners and other co-accused persons.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have falsely 2 MCRC-42796-2023 been implicated in the crime.
There is no specific allegation nor any harassment is mentioned against the present petitioners in the FIR as well as in the statement of the prosecutrix.
There was relationship between the prosecutrix and main accused Niyaz Khan.
The prosecutrix is major and went along with Niyaz Khan.
The FIR has been lodged against the petitioners with malafide intention and to wreck vengeance.
In view of the aforesaid, he has prayed for quashment of FIR and all subsequent proceedings registered against the petitioners.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the contention stating therein Vikram Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39143282/
1 that the petitioners have facilitated in commission of offence.

sentences.text: They have assisted the co-accused Niyaz Khan.
The prosecutrix in her statements have clearly alleged against the petitioners.
Therefore, at this stage the FIR could not be quashed.

As far as quashing of FIR is concerned, the same should be done at the rarest of the rare cases when there is no material available on record and continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners amounts to abuse of process of law.
However, in the present case no such circumstances exists.

The interference in the cases of quashment of the FIR can be made in very rare cases as has been considered and held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajanlal reported in 1992 Suppl. SCC 335 and in the case of Niharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in 2021 SCC OnLine 315; and in the case State of Telangana v. Habib Abdullah Jeelani and Ors reported in 2017 (2) SCC 779.

In view of the aforesaid, he has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

The law with respect to quashment of an F.I.R. is settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in large number of cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a landmark judgment in the case of Bhajanlal (supra) has laid down certain guidelines which were subsequently reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment passed in the case of Niharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. (supra),

sentences.text: Therefore, when the investigation by the police is in progress, the court should not go into the merits of the allegations in the FIR.
Police must be permitted to complete the investigation.
It would b e premature to pronounce the conclusion based on hazy facts that the complaint/FIR does not deserve to be investigated or that it amounts to abuse of process of law.

After investigation, if the investigating officer finds that there is no substance in the application made by the complainant, the investigating officer may file an appropriate report/summary before the learned Magistrate which may be considered by the learned Magistrate in accordance with the known procedure;
xiii) The power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is very wide, but conferment of wide power requires the court to be more cautious.
It casts an onerous and more diligent duty on the court;

sentences.text: When a prayer for quashing the FIR is made by the alleged 5 MCRC-42796-2023 accused and the court when it exercises the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C., only has to consider whether the allegations in the FIR disclose commission of a cognizable offence or not.

The court is not required to consider on merits whether or not the merits of the allegations make out a cognizable offence and the court has to permit the investigating agency/police to investigate the allegations in the FIR;
xvi) The aforesaid parameters would be applicable and/or the aforesaid aspects are required to be considered by the High Court while passing an interim order in a quashing petition in exercise of powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

However,
an interim order of stay of investigation during the pendency of the quashing petition can be passed with circumspection.
Such an interim order should not require to be passed routinely, casually and/or mechanically.

Normally, when the investigation is in progress and the facts are hazy and the entire evidence/material is not before the High Court, the High Court should restrain itself from passing the interim order of not to arrest or ''no coercive steps to be adopted and the accused should be relegated to apply for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. before the competent court.

The High Court shall not and as such is not justified in passing the order of not to arrest and/or ''no coercive steps either during the investigation or till the investigation is completed and/or till the final report/charge sheet is filed under Section 173 Cr.P.C., while dismissing/disposing of the quashing petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

xvii) Even in a case where the High Court is prima facie of the opinion that an exceptional case is made out for grant of interim stay of further investigation, after considering the broad parameters while exercising the powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India referred to hereinabove, the High Court has to give brief reasons why such an interim order is warranted and/or is required to be passed so that it can demonstrate the application of mind by the Court and the higher forum can consider what was weighed with the High Court while passing such an interim order.

xviii) Whenever an interim order is passed by the High Court of no coercive steps to be adopted within the aforesaid parameters, the High Court must clarify what does it mean by "no coercive 6 MCRC-42796-2023 steps to be adopted as the term" no coercive steps to be adopted can be said to be too vague and/or broad which can be misunderstood and/or misapplied."
7. The involvement of the applicants is clearly reflected in the case and their names appeared in the FIR as well as in the statement of the prosecutrix.
At this stage, this Court cannot go into the minute details of the complaint and evidence available on record.
Prima facie case is required to be seen at the time of registration of FIR.
It is settled principles of law that FIR is not an encyclopedia and cannot contain all the details particulars of the crime.
These are the matter of trial to be considered by leading appropriate evidence before the learned trial Court.
Under these circumstances, no case for quashment of FIR and the subsequent criminal proceedings is made out.

8. The petition sans merit and is accordingly dismissed.
9. Pending interlocutory application stands disposed off.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE SSL Vikram Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39143282/
